input.question: How can I go to sleep extremely hungry/thirsty yet wake up and not feel the hunger/thirst at all?
input.ground_truth: After the energy of the food you consumed is used up, your blood sugar drops and the body enters a fasting state. The liver releases small doses of glucose by breaking down glycogen to maintain your blood sugar (in your case while sleeping). So when you wake up your blood sugar is at the right level and you don't feel hungry.

But when you fall asleep, your brain kind of turns down the "I'm hungry!" or "I'm thirsty!" music for a little while. It's like how you stop noticing the tag in your shirt when you're playing and having fun.

So, when you are sleeping, you don't feel as much that you are hungry or thirsty. When you wake up, your body might remember it was hungry or thirsty, but sometimes it takes a little while for you to notice again, especially if you are busy or distracted.

It's like when you are watching your favorite cartoon and you forget you are hungry until the show is over!

But it's still good to try to eat and drink when you can, so your body stays happy and healthy.
